title: Aviation mechanic major alterations, major repairs and preventive maintenance practice questions
description: Practice questions on 14 CFR Part 43 Appendix A: what makes an alteration or repair major, and the conditions on preventive maintenance items.

questions.question: Part 43 applies to aircraft issued a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category, with some exceptions. For which products does 43.1(d)(3) say the listing of major alterations and major repairs in paragraphs (a) and (b) of appendix A is not applicable?

options.A: Products maintained only by their owner
options.B: Products not produced under an FAA approval
options.C: Products more than 20 years old
options.D: Products used only for flight training

questions.explanation: 43.1(d)(3) states: "The listing of major alterations and major repairs specified in paragraphs (a) and (b) of appendix A of this part is not applicable to products not produced under an FAA approval."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Appendix A, paragraph (a)(1), names parts and types of alterations of an airframe. Under what condition are those alterations airframe major alterations?

options.A: When they are performed by someone other than the manufacturer
options.B: When they take more than one day to complete
options.C: When they are done on an aircraft used for hire
options.D: When not listed in the aircraft specifications issued by the FAA

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(1) states that alterations of the listed parts and types, "when not listed in the aircraft specifications issued by the FAA, are airframe major alterations".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An owner plans a change to the aircraft's empty weight and empty balance. Appendix A (a)(1)(xi) lists changes to the empty weight or empty balance that result in what?

options.A: An increase in the maximum certificated weight or center of gravity limits of the aircraft
options.B: Any change of the empty weight, however small
options.C: A change that needs a new equipment list
options.D: A reduction of the aircraft's useful load

questions.explanation: Item (a)(1)(xi) reads: "Changes to the empty weight or empty balance which result in an increase in the maximum certificated weight or center of gravity limits of the aircraft."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix A (a)(1)(xiii), changes to the wing or to fixed or movable control surfaces are listed as airframe major alterations when they affect which characteristics?

options.A: Paint and finish characteristics
options.B: Stall warning characteristics
options.C: Flutter and vibration characteristics
options.D: Ground handling characteristics

questions.explanation: Item (a)(1)(xiii) reads: "Changes to the wing or to fixed or movable control surfaces which affect flutter and vibration characteristics."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Appendix A (a)(2)(i) lists the conversion of an aircraft engine from one approved model to another as a powerplant major alteration when the conversion involves what?

options.A: Any changes in compression ratio, propeller reduction gear, impeller gear ratios or the substitution of major engine parts which requires extensive rework and testing of the engine
options.B: Only a change of the model designation on the engine's data plate, with no change to the engine's parts
options.C: Only changes that increase the engine's rated power
options.D: Only changes made by a person other than the engine manufacturer

questions.explanation: Item (a)(2)(i) covers a conversion "involving any changes in compression ratio, propeller reduction gear, impeller gear ratios or the substitution of major engine parts which requires extensive rework and testing of the engine."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix A (a)(2)(ii), changes to the engine by replacing aircraft engine structural parts are a powerplant major alteration when the replacement parts are which?

options.A: Parts bought from a different parts distributor
options.B: Parts not supplied by the original manufacturer or parts not specifically approved by the Administrator
options.C: Parts that are new rather than overhauled
options.D: Parts installed by the holder of a powerplant rating

questions.explanation: Item (a)(2)(ii) reads: "Changes to the engine by replacing aircraft engine structural parts with parts not supplied by the original manufacturer or parts not specifically approved by the Administrator."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix A (a)(3), when are the listed alterations of a propeller propeller major alterations?

options.A: When the propeller has more than two blades
options.B: When the propeller is removed from the aircraft for the work
options.C: When the work is done by a repair station
options.D: When not authorized in the propeller specifications issued by the FAA

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(3) states: "The following alterations of a propeller when not authorized in the propeller specifications issued by the FAA are propeller major alterations".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix A (a)(4), which alterations of an appliance's basic design are appliance major alterations?

options.A: Any alteration of the basic design, however it is made
options.B: Only alterations requested by the aircraft owner
options.C: Alterations of the basic design not made in accordance with recommendations of the appliance manufacturer or in accordance with an FAA Airworthiness Directive
options.D: Only alterations that add weight to the appliance

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(4) states: "Alterations of the basic design not made in accordance with recommendations of the appliance manufacturer or in accordance with an FAA Airworthiness Directive are appliance major alterations."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Appendix A (a)(4) also covers communication and navigation equipment approved under type certification or a Technical Standard Order. Which changes to that equipment does it say are also major alterations?

options.A: Only changes that replace the equipment's display
options.B: Only changes made outside the equipment manufacturer's facility
options.C: Only changes that require new wiring in the aircraft
options.D: Changes that have an effect on frequency stability, noise level, sensitivity, selectivity, distortion, spurious radiation, AVC characteristics, or ability to meet environmental test conditions, and other changes that have an effect on the performance of the equipment

questions.explanation: The appendix covers changes to such equipment "that have an effect on frequency stability, noise level, sensitivity, selectivity, distortion, spurious radiation, AVC characteristics, or ability to meet environmental test conditions and other changes that have an effect on the performance of the equipment are also major alterations."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Appendix A (b)(1) lists parts and types of repairs of an airframe. What must those repairs involve to be airframe major repairs?

options.A: The strengthening, reinforcing, splicing, and manufacturing of primary structural members or their replacement, when replacement is by fabrication such as riveting or welding
options.B: Any work on the airframe that takes the aircraft out of service
options.C: Any repair that needs paint or a protective coating
options.D: Only repairs made after an accident reported to the FAA

questions.explanation: Paragraph (b)(1) covers repairs "involving the strengthening, reinforcing, splicing, and manufacturing of primary structural members or their replacement, when replacement is by fabrication such as riveting or welding, are airframe major repairs."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A shop is rebottoming a fuel tank. Appendix A (b)(1)(xxviii) lists repairing, including rebottoming, of which tanks as an airframe major repair?

options.A: Only removable fuel tanks
options.B: Removable or integral fuel tanks and oil tanks
options.C: Only integral fuel tanks, not oil tanks
options.D: Only oil tanks mounted on the engine

questions.explanation: Item (b)(1)(xxviii) reads: "Repairing, including rebottoming, of removable or integral fuel tanks and oil tanks."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Powerplant, propeller and appliance major repairs
questions.question: A shop plans a special repair to a structural engine part. Under Appendix A (b)(2)(iii), which repair methods does this listed powerplant major repair name?

options.A: Welding, plating, metalizing, or other methods
options.B: Welding only
options.C: Only methods the engine manufacturer has not approved
options.D: Only methods that require extensive testing of the engine afterward

questions.explanation: Item (b)(2)(iii) reads: "Special repairs to structural engine parts by welding, plating, metalizing, or other methods."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Preventive maintenance: the limit and item conditions
questions.question: Under Appendix A (c)(15), replacing seats or seat parts is in the preventive maintenance list with which replacement parts?

options.A: Any parts of equal or greater strength than the originals
options.B: Parts taken from any aircraft of the same category
options.C: Parts chosen by the aircraft owner
options.D: Replacement parts approved for the aircraft

questions.explanation: Item (c)(15) reads: "Replacing seats or seat parts with replacement parts approved for the aircraft, not involving disassembly of any primary structure or operating system."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Preventive maintenance: the limit and item conditions
questions.question: Under Appendix A (c)(19), replacing any cowling is in the preventive maintenance list when the work does not require what?

options.A: Removal of the engine from its mount
options.B: A ground run of the engine afterward
options.C: Removal of the propeller or disconnection of flight controls
options.D: The use of any hand tools

questions.explanation: Item (c)(19) reads: "Replacing any cowling not requiring removal of the propeller or disconnection of flight controls."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Preventive maintenance: the limit and item conditions
questions.question: An owner wants to install an anti-misfueling device that reduces the diameter of the fuel tank filler opening as preventive maintenance under Appendix A (c)(28). Which of these is one of the item's conditions?

options.A: The device is supplied by the fuel tank's manufacturer
options.B: Installation does not involve the disassembly of the existing tank filler opening
options.C: The device is installed within 30 days after an annual inspection
options.D: The aircraft is operated under part 121

questions.explanation: Item (c)(28) covers such devices "provided the specific device has been made a part of the aircraft type" certificate data by the aircraft manufacturer, "the aircraft manufacturer has provided FAA-approved instructions for installation of the specific device, and installation does not involve the disassembly of the existing tank filler opening."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Preventive maintenance: the limit and item conditions
questions.question: Under Appendix A (c)(6), lubrication is in the preventive maintenance list when it does not require disassembly other than what?

options.A: Removal of the propeller
options.B: Disconnection of flight controls
options.C: Removal of nonstructural items such as cover plates, cowlings, and fairings
options.D: Removal of any part the owner chooses

questions.explanation: Item (c)(6) reads: "Lubrication not requiring disassembly other than removal of nonstructural items such as cover plates, cowlings, and fairings."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Preventive maintenance: the limit and item conditions
questions.question: A pilot wants to replace the wheels on a small airplane as preventive maintenance. Under Appendix A (c)(18), what condition applies to replacing wheels and skis?

options.A: The new wheels must come from the original manufacturer
options.B: A mechanic must be present for the work
options.C: No weight and balance computation is involved
options.D: The work must be done at a repair station

questions.explanation: Item (c)(18) reads: "Replacing wheels and skis where no weight and balance computation is involved."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Preventive maintenance: the limit and item conditions
questions.question: A pilot makes small simple repairs to a cowling, including a small patch and reinforcement. Under Appendix A (c)(12), what must the small patches and reinforcements not do?

options.A: Change the contour so as to interfere with proper air flow
options.B: Use any material other than aluminum
options.C: Add any weight to the aircraft
options.D: Cover more than one fastener

questions.explanation: Item (c)(12) reads: "Making small simple repairs to fairings, nonstructural cover plates, cowlings, and small patches and reinforcements not changing the contour so as to interfere with proper air flow."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Preventive maintenance: balloons, primary category and avionics
questions.question: Appendix A (c)(30) covers inspection and maintenance tasks in a primary category aircraft's approved special inspection and preventive maintenance program. Under (c)(30)(i), who performs them?

options.A: Any pilot who rents the aircraft
options.B: Any person who has read the program's instructions
options.C: A student pilot who is a co-owner of the aircraft
options.D: The holder of at least a private pilot certificate issued under part 61 who is the registered owner (including co-owners) of the affected aircraft and who holds a certificate of competency for the affected aircraft

questions.explanation: Item (c)(30)(i) requires that the tasks are "performed by the holder of at least a private pilot certificate issued under part 61 of this chapter who is the registered owner (including co-owners) of the affected aircraft and who holds a certificate of competency for the affected aircraft".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Preventive maintenance: balloons, primary category and avionics
questions.question: Appendix A (c)(31) covers removing and replacing self-contained, front instrument panel-mounted navigation and communication devices that employ tray-mounted connectors. What does it require of the approved unit?

options.A: It must be installed by the unit's manufacturer
options.B: It must be designed to be readily and repeatedly removed and replaced, and pertinent instructions must be provided
options.C: It must be connected by individually soldered wires
options.D: It must be less than five years old

questions.explanation: Item (c)(31) states: "The approved unit must be designed to be readily and repeatedly removed and replaced, and pertinent instructions must be provided."
